matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can become an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one diagonal stick to intersect the V, and conversely an X can become a V by moving one diagonal away, provided the source remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V or X and a single diagonal stick can be transferred without invalidating the source character, and the resulting shape is a legal Roman numeral.
matchstick.example: Turn V into X by adding a diagonal from another character, or turn X into V by moving one diagonal to another numeral.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides; the difference tells how much the total must increase or decrease, guiding which stick moves could balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the equation, before trying any moves.
matchstick.example: If LHS=3 and RHS=26, the discrepancy is 23, so look for a move that changes the total by 23.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must stay exactly two horizontal sticks; it cannot be altered, used as a source, or broken into other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout solving; never consider moving sticks from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Do not take a horizontal stick from '=' to make a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, each affected character must still be a recognized Roman numeral or a legal operator; otherwise the move is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing any stick relocation, before accepting it.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V leaves a single diagonal, which is not a numeral, so reject that move.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a horizontal cannot become vertical or diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When deciding where to place a moved stick; ensure the target shape requires that orientation.
matchstick.example: You cannot use a vertical stick to form the diagonal part of an X.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., '+' to '-') is allowed only if the new symbol is a legal operator in the puzzle; the transformation must be achievable by moving a stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' yields '-', which is a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to verify equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, before final acceptance.
matchstick.example: After turning '+' into '-', recompute RHS as XV - XI.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign while providing a vertical stick that can be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and a vertical stick is needed for another character.
matchstick.example: Move the vertical stick from '+' to XI, turning '+' into '-' and XI into XII.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved from one character to another, simultaneously decreasing the source’s value and increasing the destination’s value, which can balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a net change that can be achieved by moving a stick between two characters.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to XI while converting '+' to '-' reduces RHS by 22 and adds 1, achieving the needed change.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick addition creates extra I (value +1)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a numeral creates an additional ‘I’, raising its value by 1 without breaking the original character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick is available and a numeral can accept an extra I (e.g., turning I into II, or adding a new I after a numeral).
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to XI yields XII, increasing its value from 11 to 12.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets that matchsticks retain their orientation and imagines rotating sticks arbitrarily.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly check that the orientation of the moved stick matches the required orientation of the target shape.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the rule that the equality sign must stay unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the '=' sign as immutable; never move sticks from or to it.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model does not verify that the source or destination character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each hypothetical move, validate that both characters are still legal symbols.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric balance and forgets operator validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure any operator transformation yields a legal operator (+, -, =).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model jumps to transformations without a guiding numeric target.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the numeric discrepancy first and use it to guide which sticks to move.
